title: Stop Using AI to Get Rid of Customers (Yeah, Really)
excerpt: Everyone's obsessed with AI deflection — but you're doing it wrong if your goal is to keep people away from humans.

content.text: So I've been watching the AI automation conversation, and there's this thing that's been bugging me. Everyone's talking about call deflection like it's the whole point — like the goal is to get as many customers as possible to NOT talk to a human. And look, I get it. Labor costs are real, and AI can handle stuff 24/7 without complaining. But here's what nobody's really saying out loud: if your main metric for success is 'how many calls did we keep away from people,' you're measuring the wrong thing. And you're probably losing customers.

Let me be direct: AI customer support automation is legitimately useful. But the frame that's gotten popular — 'deflection' — that's the problem. Deflection sounds like you're keeping people out. And honestly? Most customers can feel that. They want their problem solved. They don't want to feel like they're being filtered out or stuck in a bot loop until they give up.

The smarter way to think about this is containment — but not the kind where you're trying to avoid human contact. Real containment means solving the problem the customer has, however it needs to be solved. Sometimes that's AI. Sometimes that's getting them to a person fast. The goal is resolution, not deflection.
Here's what matters: customers who can't get help abandon you. AI that solves their actual problem keeps them. Those are two totally different things.

items: Routine stuff that's genuinely repetitive — password resets, account lookups, basic billing questions. If a human is doing the same exact thing 100 times a day, automate it.
High-volume, low-complexity requests — appointment scheduling, order status checks, simple FAQs. AI is actually great at this.
After-hours coverage — if you're closed at 2 AM and someone needs an answer, AI handling it is better than radio silence.
Triage and context-gathering — have AI collect information before handing off to a human. That saves time for everyone.
Things that are genuinely bottlenecks in your process — if your team is drowning in a specific type of call, automate that one thing first.

content.text: What you shouldn't automate? Anything where a customer is frustrated, confused, or needs judgment. Complex problems. Complaints. Anything that requires empathy or nuance. Yeah, an AI might *technically* handle it. But humans do it better. And your customer will know the difference.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Stop measuring success by 'calls deflected.' Start measuring by 'problems solved on first contact' and 'customer satisfaction.' If your AI is good, those numbers will be great — and customers will actually like talking to you. Use AI to make your team faster and smarter, not to keep people away.

The businesses winning right now aren't the ones obsessed with cutting humans out. They're the ones using AI to make their humans better at their jobs. AI handles the repetitive stuff so your team can focus on the conversations that actually matter. That's the move.
